resources.string: DSH Mobile mirrors the DeepSeek Harness running on your computer.

Connect using the computer\'s IP address instead of its name, or start the harness with --trusted-host.
Enter the computer\'s IP address and a port between 1 and 65535.
Nothing answered at %1$s. Usually the computer\'s firewall is blocking incoming connections on port %2$d — allow it and try again. Some routers also stop Wi-Fi devices from reaching wired ones.
%1$s refused the connection. The harness only listens on the computer itself unless LAN mode is enabled — enable it and restart the harness. If you changed the port, check it matches.
No device on this network answers to “%1$s”. Use the computer\'s IP address instead — find it with ipconfig on Windows, ip addr on Linux, or ifconfig on macOS.
Something answered at %1$s, but it is not a DeepSeek Harness. Check the port the harness printed when it started.

%1$s answered, but the secure (HTTPS) connection failed. If your proxy uses a local certificate authority, install its CA certificate on this phone — and if the address does not actually serve HTTPS, connect without https://.

%1$s answered, but its event stream would not open. A VPN or private-DNS proxy on this phone can block WebSocket connections — turn it off and try again. Android can also freeze the app itself right after launch — force-stop the app and try again.
Harness version %1$s may be incompatible with this app (built for %2$s).
The harness prints a link when it starts. Paste that link — or just its token — here. It changes every time the harness restarts.
The harness did not accept that token. It changes on every restart, so check the most recent startup line.

Try connecting first, then sign in.

Full coding agent with file editing, shell, file and web search, skills, planning, goals, subagents, and workflows.
All Standard mode capabilities, with tools exposed through the Code Mode SDK so the model can combine multi-step operations in one TypeScript program.
Two-tool coding agent with persistent bash and str_replace_editor.
Built for creating custom agent presets, with all Standard mode capabilities plus runtime inspection, plugin experiments, and preset-authoring guidance.

A relay checks that it is you, and nothing else. Once paired, this device can run commands on that computer, exactly as a terminal on it could.
Relays you pair with appear here.
No relays found yet. Install the dsh-relay plugin into the harness web profile and restart it, then look again.
Open /relay/pair on the computer running the harness, then scan the code it shows or type it in.
Auto-connect to a paired relay on Wi-Fi
The relay no longer accepts this device\'s token. It may have expired, or been revoked from the relay\'s device list. Pair again to be issued a new one.

%1$s presented a different key from the one saved when this device paired. That happens when a relay regenerates its certificate after moving networks — but it looks the same as something else answering at that address. Pair again only if you were expecting it.
On the computer running the harness, open /relay/pair. It shows a QR code and an eight-digit code; either one works, and both expire after a few minutes.
Point the camera at the code on the relay\'s pairing page
The scanned code carries this relay\'s key, so it is checked before anything is sent.
A typed address carries no key, so this trusts whatever answers the first time. Scanning the QR code checks it instead.
This address is not encrypted, so the token and everything you send travel in the clear.
That is not a relay pairing code.
That code comes from a newer relay (version %1$d) than this app understands. Update DSH Mobile.
That code has expired. Reload the relay\'s pairing page for a new one.
The relay refused that code. Codes work once and expire after a few minutes — reload the pairing page and try the new one.
Too many attempts. Wait %1$d seconds and try again.
%1$s answered, but it does not accept pairing. Use the address the relay printed when it started, not the harness\'s own.
Could not reach %1$s. Check the address, and that the relay is running and reachable from this phone.
The key at %1$s is not the one this code names. Do not pair — something else may be answering at that address.
Enter the relay address, including https://
Enter the code shown on the relay\'s pairing page.
A relay is running here, but it only answers to addresses it already knows. Add %1$s to publicHostnames in the relay\'s cordis.patch.yml on that computer, then restart it.

%1$s is a relay, but it refuses requests addressed this way — the code was never read. Add that address to publicHostnames in the relay\'s cordis.patch.yml and restart, or reach the relay by an address it already knows.
